title: Orange rainfall warning up in parts of Metro Manila, other provinces

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Parts of Metro Manila and other provinces were placed under orange and yellow rainfall warnings on Wednesday morning as the southwest monsoon or habagat persists, the state weather bureau said.

In its heavy rainfall advisory on Wednesday issued at 8 a.m., the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said orange rainfall warning is up in the following areas:

items: Metro Manila – Valenzuela, Caloocan, Malabon, Quezon City, Navotas, Manila, Mandaluyong, San Juan, Marikina
Zambales – San Antonio, Olongapo, Castillejos, Subic

blocks.text: Under orange warning, 15 mm and 30 mm rainfall is expected within one hour and can continue in the next two hours. For every hour, this volume of rainfall can fill four 20-gallon water containers per square meter.
Moreover, a yellow warning was raised over the following areas:

items: Metro Manila – Las Pinas, Muntinlupa, Paranaque, Taguig, Makati, Pasig, Pasay, Pateros
Bulacan – Bocaue, Balagtas, Bulakan, Guiguinto, Malolos, Paombong, Hagonoy, San Jose del Monte, Marilao, Meycauayan
Pampanga – Masantol, Macabebe, Sasmuan, Lubao, Floridablanca
Zambales – Botolan, Cabangan, Candelaria, Iba, Masinloc, Palauig, Santa Cruz, San Felipe, San Marcelino, San Narciso
Cavite – Bacoor, Cavite City, Imus, Kawit, Noveleta

blocks.text: Areas under yellow warning tend to experience rainfall between 7.5 mm and 15 mm within one hour and can continue in the next two hours.
Meanwhile, Pagasa said that light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains are also expected over Quezon, Laguna and parts of Nueva Ecija within the next three hours.

Light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains are also affecting parts of Pampanga, Tarlac, Cavite, Batangas, Rizal and Bulacan, which may persist for the next three hours and affect nearby areas. /jpv
